_comment: Runtime component registry. Fetched by the app at setup and on demand, so new components and revised site tuning ship without an app release. Keep this file valid JSON — a broken manifest blocks first-run setup for every user.

components.name: HQ Pack
components.summary: Merges video and audio, converts to MP3, embeds subtitles.

platforms._comment: Repacked from the BtbN n9.0 linux64-gpl static build and self-hosted, exactly as the Windows zip is repacked from gyan.dev. Version parity with the Windows pack (9.0.1) is deliberate: one ffmpeg behaviour to reason about across platforms. Bigger than Windows because the Linux build is not UPX-packed.

components.name: Download engine
components.summary: The extractor that talks to ~1800 sites.
components._comment: sha256 is null by design: this tracks yt-dlp's rolling latest release, so the hash changes on their schedule, not ours. Integrity comes from HTTPS plus a post-download `--version` execution check. Pinning a hash here would break setup every time yt-dlp ships.

platforms._comment: The Linux build is a separate asset with a different name and no .exe suffix. sha256 is null for the same reason it is null above: this tracks yt-dlp rolling latest.

siteProfiles._comment: Per-site tuning applied to yt-dlp invocations. Not extractors - yt-dlp already supports these sites. Add an entry only for tuning that cannot be discovered at runtime: a host needing nothing but impersonation does NOT belong here, because the probe now finds that itself on a bot wall, and a hostname in a public file says which sites were asked for.

domains._comment: Maps a domain with no working extractor to the optional component that adds one. Empty for now — the request pipeline fills it as real cases arrive.

_plugins_comment: yt-dlp extractor plugins, delivered without an app release. Each entry needs id, name, version, summary, an https url and a lowercase-hex sha256, which is checked before the file is written anywhere yt-dlp loads from. This is executable code on a user machine: treat it like shipping a binary, never like shipping config, and never populate it from anything a user supplied. Keep ids generic - an id should describe the mechanism, not name a site.
